title: Matching

constraints.text: N ≤ 21 men and women, compatibility matrix

explanation: N ≤ 21 screams bitmask. Match men in order; the set of used women determines which man is next (popcount).
traps: Adding the man index as an extra dimension multiplies the work by 21 for nothing.

extraLayers.prompt: What should the DP state represent?

options.text: dp[mask] = number of ways to pair the first popcount(mask) men with exactly the women in mask
dp[i][mask] = ways to pair the first i men with women mask
options.why: Correct but redundant: i = popcount(mask), and N·2^N·N ≈ 9e8 is too slow.

options.text: dp[i][j] = ways man i is paired with woman j
options.why: Pairs aren't independent; women can't be reused.
Matching finds one perfect matching; this asks how many there are.

extraLayers.explanation: Process men in a fixed order; the used-women set is all you need, and it tells you the next man.

extraLayers.prompt: Given that state, which transition is right?

options.text: Let i = popcount(mask) − 1 (the man being placed); dp[mask] = Σ over women w ∈ mask with compat[i][w] of dp[mask \ {w}]
dp[mask] = Σ over all w ∈ mask of dp[mask \ {w}]
dp[mask] = max over w of dp[mask \ {w}] + 1
dp[mask] = Π over w ∈ mask of compat[popcount][w]

extraLayers.explanation: The last man placed took some compatible woman w; remove her and count the rest.
